q: Which IRS form does a corporation file to elect to be taxed as an S corporation?
why: Form 2553 is the S corporation election. Form 8832 is the entity classification election, SS-4 requests an EIN, and 1120 is the C corporation return.

q: Shareholders of an S corporation are taxed on their share of the company's income:
c: only when it is paid out as dividends
only after the corporation pays its own tax
whether or not it is distributed to them
only if it exceeds the company's retained earnings
why: S corporation income passes through on Schedule K-1 and is taxable to shareholders in the year earned, whether or not it is distributed. The entity generally pays no federal income tax.

q: A general partnership closes owing a supplier $60,000. The partnership has three general partners. What is the most the supplier can collect from any single partner?
why: Under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act, general partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership debts. Once the partnership's assets are exhausted, a creditor can collect the entire debt from any one partner, and that partner can then seek contribution from the others.

q: Which owners have no management authority and risk losing only the amount they invested?
why: Limited partners stay out of management, and their liability is capped at their investment. General partners manage the business and carry unlimited liability.

q: A contractor wants coverage for a building under construction against every cause of loss except those specifically excluded. Which policy fits best?
why: An all-risk (special form) builder's risk policy covers every peril not excluded. A named-peril policy covers only the perils it lists.

q: A contractor's commercial general liability policy would normally respond to which claim?
c: An employee's back injury from lifting drywall
Theft of the contractor's excavator from the yard
A neighbor injured by debris falling from the jobsite
A design error in drawings the contractor prepared
why: CGL covers bodily injury and property damage to third parties. Employee injuries fall under workers' comp, equipment theft under an inland marine floater, and design errors under professional liability.

q: Which coverage protects mobile construction equipment while it is in storage, in transit, or at a temporary jobsite?
why: An equipment floater is an inland marine policy that follows movable equipment wherever it is. Builder's risk covers the structure being built.

q: Under federal rules, an employer becomes liable for FUTA tax if it had at least one employee during some part of a day in how many different weeks of the current or prior calendar year?
why: The FUTA test is met by paying $1,500 or more in wages in any calendar quarter, or by having an employee in 20 or more different weeks in the current or prior year.

q: In a contract surety bond, the contractor whose performance is guaranteed is called the:
why: The principal (contractor) owes the obligation, the obligee (owner) is protected, and the surety guarantees performance and can seek reimbursement from the principal.

q: Which bond assures the owner that a bidder will sign the contract at its bid price and furnish the required performance and payment bonds?
why: A bid bond backs the bidder's promise to enter the contract and provide the required bonds. If the bidder refuses, the surety compensates the owner up to the bond amount.

q: Under the Miller Act as applied in the FAR, performance and payment bonds are required on federal construction contracts exceeding:
why: The original $100,000 statutory threshold has been inflation-adjusted to $150,000, and the 2025 FAR inflation update left the bond threshold unchanged.

q: A federal construction contract is awarded for $4,000,000. Absent a contracting officer determination that it is impractical, the payment bond's penal amount should be:
why: Since the 1999 amendments, federal payment bonds equal 100% of the original contract price. The old 50%/40%/$2.5 million sliding scale no longer applies.

q: Which bond guarantees for a stated period after completion that no defects in workmanship or materials will appear?
why: A maintenance (warranty) bond covers defects that appear in a set period after completion. A performance bond covers completing the work itself.

q: A change to the bidding documents issued to all bidders before bids are due is called a(n):
why: Addenda modify the bid documents before bids are opened and become part of the contract documents. Change orders and directives modify an executed contract.

q: Several contractors secretly agree on which of them will submit the low bid on a public project. This is:
why: Bid rigging is collusion among competitors to set the outcome of a bid and is a federal antitrust crime. Bid shopping is a contractor shopping one sub's price to others.

q: Which of the following is part of labor burden?
c: Employer's share of Social Security and Medicare
Rental cost of a scissor lift
why: Labor burden is the employer's cost on top of wages: payroll taxes, workers' comp, insurance and benefits. Base wages, equipment and office rent are other cost categories.

q: Which cost is company (general) overhead rather than project overhead?
c: Accounting fees for the main office
why: Company overhead is incurred whether or not jobs are running, such as office rent, accounting and admin salaries. Trailers, toilets and permits are job-specific costs.

q: Using the square-foot method, what is the estimated cost of a 2,400 sq ft building at $140 per square foot?
why: The square-foot method multiplies floor area by a unit cost: 2,400 sq ft x $140/sq ft = $336,000.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the required elements of a valid contract?
why: A valid contract needs offer and acceptance, consideration, competent parties and a legal purpose. Notarization is not a general requirement.

q: An owner offers a remodel contract for $80,000. The contractor replies that it will do the work for $86,000. Legally, the contractor's reply is:
c: a counteroffer that rejects the original offer
an acceptance with a price adjustment
why: Acceptance must match the offer's terms. Changing the price makes the reply a counteroffer, which ends the original offer and creates a new one.

q: A $200,000 lump-sum contract carries 10% retainage. The work is 90% complete and all progress payments to date have been made. How much remains to be paid to the contractor?
why: Earned to date is $180,000, less 10% retainage ($18,000), so $162,000 has been paid. The balance is $200,000 - $162,000 = $38,000.

q: Under AIA A201-2017, unless the contract provides otherwise, who secures and pays for the building permit?
why: A201 assigns the building permit and related permits, fees and licenses to the contractor. The owner handles approvals, easements and assessments.

q: An owner pays a progress payment one day late, and the contractor abandons the job permanently. Who has committed a material breach?
c: The contractor, by abandoning the work
why: A one-day payment delay is normally an immaterial breach, which supports damages but not termination. Abandoning the work goes to the heart of the contract and is a material breach.

q: A contract requires the contractor to pay the owner $750 for each calendar day the project finishes late. This provision is an example of:
why: Liquidated damages are a delay amount agreed in advance; they must be a reasonable estimate of actual loss, not a penalty.

q: An owner with only preliminary drawings wants to start work on a site where the amount of rock excavation is unknown. Which contract type best fits the excavation work?
why: Unit-price contracts pay a set rate times the actual measured quantity, so they suit work whose quantity cannot be determined in advance.

q: A client upgrades flooring and the cost exceeds the flooring allowance in the contract. How should the contractor handle the difference?
c: Absorb the overage as part of the original price
Bill the overage on the final invoice without documentation
Issue a written change order adjusting the contract sum
why: When an allowance is exceeded, the contract sum is adjusted by a written, signed change order.

q: Changes to the bidding documents issued before bids are opened are called:
why: Addenda modify the bid documents before bid opening or contract execution; change orders modify the contract after award.

q: Which dispute resolution method produces a decision that legally binds the parties?
why: An arbitrator issues a binding award; a mediator only helps the parties reach their own agreement.

q: A contract clause is ambiguous and neither party can show what was intended. A court will usually interpret it:
c: Against the party that drafted the contract
In favor of the party that drafted the contract
In favor of the owner in all cases
why: Ambiguities are construed against the drafter, who had the chance to write the language clearly.

q: The amount of time an activity can slip without delaying the project completion date is called:
why: Float (slack) is scheduling leeway; activities on the critical path have zero float.

q: What is the main limitation of a bar chart (Gantt) schedule compared with a CPM schedule?
c: It does not show dependencies between activities
It cannot be tied to calendar dates
why: Bar charts show durations and timing, but only CPM shows the logical links that reveal how one delay affects the finish date.

q: On a project using AIA contract documents, who certifies the contractor's application for payment?
why: The architect reviews each pay application and certifies the amount due before the owner pays.

q: Which record best supports a contractor's request for a time extension due to rain delays?
why: Daily logs record weather and its effect on work each day, providing evidence for delay claims.

q: Under the FLSA, what is the earliest time of day a 15-year-old may begin work?
why: 14- and 15-year-olds may work only between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 1 through Labor Day).

q: Under federal law, what is the longest an employer may take to report a new hire to the state directory if the state has not set a shorter deadline?
why: Federal law sets a 20-day maximum; states may require faster reporting.

q: An employee starts work on Monday. By when must the employer complete Section 2 of Form I-9?
c: By the end of the first pay period
Within 3 business days after the first day of work
why: Section 1 is due by the first day of work; the employer must examine documents and complete Section 2 within 3 business days.

q: A worker was hired 5 years ago and quit last month. How long must the employer keep his Form I-9?
c: Until 1 year after his last day of work
Until 3 years after his last day of work
why: Retention is 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, whichever is later; here the 1-year date is later.

q: For Form I-9 purposes, an unrestricted Social Security card establishes:
why: It is a List C document and must be paired with a List B identity document such as a driver's license.

q: A 17-year-old new hire may be paid the $4.25 youth minimum wage for how long?
why: Employees under 20 may receive the youth wage only during their first 90 consecutive calendar days of employment.

q: A carpenter works 37 hours one week and 43 hours the next to make up missed time. How is he paid for the second week under the FLSA?
c: 43 hours at straight time, since the two weeks average 40
40 hours at straight time plus 3 hours at 1.5 times the regular rate
43 hours at 1.5 times the regular rate
40 hours at straight time; the extra 3 hours are unpaid
why: Each workweek stands alone and hours cannot be averaged, so hours over 40 in a week earn overtime.

q: An hourly worker stays 3 extra hours without his supervisor's approval, violating company policy. Under the FLSA, the employer:
c: Must pay the overtime but may discipline the worker
May refuse to pay because it was unauthorized
May give comp time next month instead
why: Work the employer suffers or permits is compensable; policy violations can be handled through discipline, not by withholding pay.

q: Title I of the ADA applies to employers with at least how many employees?
why: ADA employment provisions cover employers with 15 or more employees.

q: An eligible employee requests FMLA leave to care for a newly adopted child. How much job-protected leave must a covered employer allow?
why: The FMLA provides up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period, with health coverage maintained.

q: An employer becomes liable for FUTA tax if it had at least one employee during some part of a day in how many weeks of the year?
why: The FUTA test is 20 or more weeks with an employee, or $1,500 in wages in any calendar quarter.

q: An employee is admitted to the hospital overnight after a fall on a jobsite. Within how many hours must the employer report it to OSHA?
why: Any in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye must be reported within 24 hours; a fatality within 8 hours.

q: How long must OSHA Forms 300, 300A and 301 be kept?
c: 5 years after the end of the year they cover
3 years after the end of the year they cover
why: Injury and illness records are kept for 5 years following the end of the calendar year they cover.

q: Which OSHA form is the Injury and Illness Incident Report, which must be completed within 7 calendar days?
why: Form 301 gives the details of each case; Form 300 is the log and Form 300A is the annual summary.

q: Which statement about OSHA civil penalty amounts is correct?
c: They are fixed by statute at $7,000 per serious violation
They are mandatory amounts OSHA cannot reduce
They apply only to willful violations
They are maximums adjusted for inflation each year
why: OSHA's maximum penalties have been adjusted for inflation since 2016 and are now updated every January. They are ceilings, and OSHA can reduce a proposed penalty based on factors such as employer size, good faith and history.

q: An OSHA inspection triggered by a worker fatality is classified as:
why: Unprogrammed inspections respond to events such as fatalities, complaints, referrals and imminent danger.

q: NPDES construction stormwater permit coverage is required when land disturbance reaches at least:
why: Disturbing 1 acre or more, or less as part of a larger common plan of 1 acre or more, requires permit coverage and a SWPPP.

q: Under the asbestos NESHAP, written notification of a planned demolition must be submitted at least how far in advance?
why: Notice is due at least 10 working days before demolition, after a thorough asbestos inspection.

q: In a 1965 house, EPA lead-safe work practice rules apply to interior renovation that disturbs more than how much painted surface per room?
why: The minor-repair exemption covers up to 6 sq ft per room inside and 20 sq ft outside; beyond that the RRP rule applies.

q: How long must a renovator keep proof that the Renovate Right lead pamphlet was delivered?
why: RRP records, including pamphlet acknowledgments, must be kept for 3 years after the renovation is completed.

q: A contractor has current assets of $80,000, of which $20,000 is inventory, and current liabilities of $40,000. What is the quick ratio?
why: Quick ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = ($80,000 − $20,000) ÷ $40,000 = 1.50.

q: A company reports total debt of $90,000 and total assets of $120,000. What is its debt ratio?
why: Debt ratio = total debt ÷ total assets = $90,000 ÷ $120,000 = 0.75.

q: Which equation describes the balance sheet?
why: Everything the company owns (assets) is financed either by creditors (liabilities) or by the owners (equity).

q: An excavator was financed on a five-year note, and the remaining balance will be paid off in four months. How should that balance appear on the balance sheet?
why: Any obligation due within the next 12 months is a current liability, whatever the original term of the loan.

q: A supplier invoice for $2,500 carries terms of 2/10 net 30. How much should the contractor pay if paying within 10 days?
why: 2/10 net 30 gives a 2% discount for payment within 10 days: $2,500 × 0.98 = $2,450.

q: A skid steer costs $48,000, has an estimated salvage value of $8,000 and a useful life of 5 years. What is the annual straight-line depreciation?
Which accounting method records income when it is earned and expenses when they are incurred, whether or not cash has changed hands?
why: The accrual method matches revenue with the costs that produced it, unlike the cash method, which waits for money to be received or paid.

q: Under the federal Prompt Payment Act, how soon must a prime contractor on a federal construction job pay a subcontractor after receiving payment from the government?
why: Primes must pay subs for satisfactory work within 7 days of receiving government payment, or owe interest.

q: By what date must an employer give employees their Form W-2 for the prior year?
why: W-2s are due to employees, and to the SSA, by January 31.

q: An employee wants to keep claiming exemption from federal income tax withholding. By when must a new Form W-4 be submitted each year?
why: An exempt W-4 expires each year, and the employee must give a new one by February 15 to continue the exemption.

q: What is the regular Medicare tax rate that both the employer and the employee pay on wages?
why: Medicare is 1.45% each for employer and employee (2.9% combined). Social Security is 6.2% each, up to the wage base.

q: An employer's total Form 941 tax liability during its lookback period was $42,000. What federal deposit schedule applies?
why: A lookback-period liability of $50,000 or less makes the employer a monthly depositor; more than $50,000 means semiweekly.

q: A payroll tax deposit is made 20 days late. What IRS failure-to-deposit penalty rate applies?
why: The penalty is 2% for 1-5 days late, 5% for 6-15 days and 10% for more than 15 days (15% after an unanswered IRS notice).

q: An employer's accumulated FUTA liability for the quarter is $650. When is the deposit due?
c: By the last day of the month after the quarter ends
By the 15th of the next month
why: Once FUTA liability exceeds $500, it must be deposited by the last day of the month after the quarter. Smaller amounts carry over to the next quarter.

q: What is the gross FUTA tax rate and the wage base it applies to?
why: FUTA is 6.0% of the first $7,000 of each employee's wages. A state unemployment credit of up to 5.4% usually brings the net rate to 0.6%.

q: A prime contractor pays an unincorporated HVAC subcontractor $10,000 for services during the year. Which IRS form reports this payment?
why: Payments for services to a non-employee who is not a corporation are reported on Form 1099-NEC once they reach the annual threshold.

q: At minimum, how long must an employer keep employment tax records?
why: The IRS requires employment tax records to be kept at least 4 years after the tax is due or paid, whichever is later.

q: Under EPA's RRP Rule, when must a renovator give the owner of a pre-1978 home the 'Renovate Right' pamphlet?
c: Within 30 days after the work ends
No more than 60 days before work begins
Only if lead hazards are found
why: Pre-renovation education means delivering the pamphlet no more than 60 days before starting and documenting that it was received.

q: Which term describes work designed to permanently eliminate lead-based paint hazards?
why: Abatement is aimed at permanent elimination of lead hazards. Interim controls and ordinary renovation are temporary or incidental.

q: How is gross profit calculated on a contractor's income statement?
c: Revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct job costs)
why: Gross profit is revenue less direct job costs. Subtracting overhead and other expenses then gives net income.

q: Which contract type pays the contractor its actual allowable costs plus an agreed fee?
why: Cost-plus contracts reimburse actual costs and add a fixed or percentage fee, instead of paying a set price.

q: A sole proprietor who has operated without employees hires her first employee. What must she now obtain from the IRS?
why: A sole proprietor without employees may use her SSN, but once she has employees she needs an EIN for payroll tax filings.

q: A profitable sole proprietor has no tax withheld on business income. What should he do to avoid an underpayment penalty?
c: Make quarterly estimated payments using Form 1040-ES
why: Self-employed people with no withholding pay income and self-employment tax through quarterly estimated payments.

q: Which of the following is NOT a source document?
why: Source documents are the papers that prove a transaction happened. Cash itself is an asset, not evidence of a transaction.

q: Without using any reduction allowed by the code, the net free ventilating area of an enclosed attic must be at least what fraction of the vented space?
why: The base requirement is 1/150; 1/300 is allowed only when high/low vent split and vapor retarder conditions are met.

q: What is the minimum bearing length for the end of a ceiling joist resting on a wood top plate?
why: Joists and rafters need 1-1/2 in of bearing on wood or metal; 3 in is required on masonry or concrete.

q: With no soil investigation, what presumptive allowable bearing pressure may be used for silty clay?
why: Clays and silts (CL, ML, MH, CH) carry a presumptive value of 1,500 psf.

q: What presumptive allowable foundation pressure applies to sandy gravel (GW or GP)?
why: Sandy gravel and gravel are assigned 3,000 psf; 4,000 is for sedimentary rock and 12,000 for crystalline bedrock.

q: Which occupant load factor does the IBC assign to a commercial kitchen?
why: Commercial kitchens are figured at 200 gross sq ft per occupant, with fractional results rounded up.

q: Below what oxygen concentration is an atmosphere considered oxygen deficient?
why: Less than 19.5% oxygen is deficient; more than 23.5% is enriched. Normal air is about 20.9%.

q: Unless designed by a qualified person with a safety factor of two, an anchorage for personal fall arrest must support at least how much per attached worker?
why: 1926.502(d)(15) requires 5,000 lb per attached employee (or a qualified-person design with a safety factor of two); 5,400 lb is the separate lifeline anchorage figure in 1926.104(b).

q: How wide must driveways between and around outdoor combustible storage piles be?
why: OSHA requires driveways at least 15 ft wide, kept clear, forming grid units no larger than 50 x 150 ft.

q: A stairway or ladder is required at a personnel access point when the break in elevation is at least:
why: Breaks in elevation of 19 in or more need a stairway or ladder unless a ramp, runway, embankment or hoist is provided.

q: Besides daily inspections, when must a competent person re-inspect an open excavation?
c: Only at the start of each work week
After every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event
Only when the depth exceeds 20 ft
Only after an OSHA compliance visit
why: Excavations must be inspected daily and again after rainstorms or any occurrence that increases the hazard.

q: An employer must have a written emergency action plan once it has at least how many employees?
why: Employers with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally, so a written plan is required at 11 or more.

q: What minimum clearance to combustible material must be kept at the sides of a temporary radiant-type heater?
why: Radiant room heaters need 36 in of side clearance; circulating types need only 12 in.

q: What Medicare tax rate is withheld from an employee's wages up to $200,000 in a year?
why: The employee pays 1.45% and the employer matches it; 2.9% is the combined total and 0.9% is the additional tax above $200,000.

q: How must a corporation with a sizable quarterly liability make its federal payroll tax deposits?
c: Mail a check with a Form 8109 coupon
Pay in cash at a local IRS office
Attach the payment to Form W-3
Electronic funds transfer, such as EFTPS
why: Paper deposit coupons ended in 2011; all federal tax deposits must be made electronically.

q: An employer is a monthly depositor if its employment taxes in the lookback period totaled:
why: $50,000 or less in the lookback period means monthly deposits; more than that means semiweekly.

q: What failure-to-deposit penalty applies to a payroll tax deposit made more than 15 days late (before an IRS notice)?
why: The tiers are 2% (1-5 days), 5% (6-15 days), 10% (over 15 days) and 15% after an unpaid notice.

q: When accumulated FUTA liability passes $500 at the end of a calendar quarter, when is the deposit due?
c: The last day of the month after the quarter ends
why: FUTA over $500 is deposited by the end of the month following the quarter; Form 940 is filed annually.

q: On a $5.1 million federal construction contract, the Miller Act payment bond normally must be:
why: Since 1999 the payment bond equals 100% of the contract price unless the contracting officer finds that impractical.

q: Which bond guarantees that a bidder, if awarded the job, will sign the contract and furnish the required bonds?
why: A bid bond protects the owner if the selected bidder refuses to enter the contract or provide bonds.

q: Which gross receipts limit determines whether a small contractor may use the completed-contract method for tax purposes?
why: The TCJA raised the limit from $10 million to $25 million indexed ($31 million for 2025), based on the prior 3-year average.

q: By what date must a contractor give subcontractors their copies of Form 1099-NEC?
why: Form 1099-NEC is due to recipients (and to the IRS) by January 31.

q: Which business may use the owner's SSN instead of obtaining an EIN?
c: A single-member LLC with three employees
A sole proprietorship with no employees and no excise or pension filings
why: Sole proprietors and single-member LLCs need an EIN once they have employees; corporations and partnerships always need one.

q: A non-exempt employee works 3 hours of overtime without the required supervisor approval. What must the employer do?
c: Refuse to pay for the unauthorized hours
Pay the hours at the overtime rate, and may discipline the employee
Pay the hours at straight time only
Convert the hours to unpaid comp time
why: Work the employer suffers or permits must be paid; policy violations are handled by discipline, not by withholding wages.

q: A federal NPDES stormwater permit is required for construction activity that disturbs at least:
why: Disturbing 1 acre or more, or less if part of a larger common plan of 1 acre or more, triggers permit coverage.

q: Manual fire alarm boxes must be located no more than what distance from the entrance to each exit?
why: Pull stations go within 5 ft of each exit entrance, mounted 42-48 in above the floor.

q: When fully open, a door in the means of egress may reduce the required egress width by no more than:
why: A fully opened door may project at most 7 in into the required width, and no more than half at any position.

q: An unsurcharged landscape retaining wall is exempt from a building permit if its height, from bottom of footing to top of wall, does not exceed:
why: Walls over 4 ft, or any wall supporting a surcharge or impounding flammable liquids, need a permit.

q: A building under construction will be 48 ft tall and is 20 ft from the lot line. What pedestrian protection is required?
c: A barrier and a covered walkway
why: 20 ft falls between 1/4 (12 ft) and 1/2 (24 ft) of the height, which requires a barrier.

q: What are the minimum size requirements for an enclosed fire service access elevator lobby?
why: The lobby must be at least 150 sq ft with no dimension under 8 ft so firefighters can stage.

q: Where ramp handrails are not continuous between runs, how far must they extend horizontally beyond the top and bottom of each run?
why: Ramp handrail extensions must be at least 12 in at both the top and the bottom.

q: What is the maximum live-load deflection allowed for a floor member?
why: Floor members are limited to L/360 under live load; L/240 applies to total load.

q: Under the IBC, footings must be stepped where the ground surface slopes more than:
why: IBC 1809.3 keeps footing tops level, allows the bottom to slope no more than 1:10, and requires stepped footings where the ground slopes more than 1 in 10 (10%).

q: A notch at the end of a solid sawn floor joist may not exceed what portion of the joist depth?
why: End notches are limited to 1/4 of the depth; notches elsewhere are limited to 1/6.

q: At what maximum spacing must drip edge be mechanically fastened to the roof deck?
why: Drip edge is fastened no more than 12 in apart, with 2 in laps and 2 in onto the deck.

q: How is drip edge layered with underlayment on a shingle roof?
c: Over the underlayment at both eaves and rakes
Under the underlayment at eaves and over it at rakes
Under the underlayment at both eaves and rakes
Over the underlayment at eaves and under it at rakes
why: At eaves the underlayment laps over the drip edge to shed water; at rakes the drip edge goes on top.

q: Corner guards protecting fireproofing on columns exposed to forklift traffic must extend at least how high above the finished floor?
why: Impact protection must reach at least 5 ft above the floor, or higher if needed for full protection.

q: A masonry chimney must extend at least how far above the highest point where it passes through the roof?
why: The 3-2-10 rule: 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.

q: A non-circular Type I handrail must have a perimeter dimension within what range?
why: Non-circular Type I rails need a 4 to 6-1/4 in perimeter and a cross section of no more than 2-1/4 in.

q: A pile standing unbraced in water may be considered laterally supported at what depth into stiff soil?
why: Lateral support may be assumed 5 ft into stiff soil or 10 ft into soft soil.

q: What minimum illumination is required at the walking surface of a means of egress while the building is occupied?
why: Egress paths need at least 1 footcandle (11 lux) at the floor.

q: During construction, a temporary or permanent stairway is required once the building rises more than what height above the lowest fire department vehicle access?
why: Above 40 ft, a stair must be provided and kept within one floor of the highest secured deck.

q: Regardless of airport proximity, FAA notice is required for a crane or structure taller than what height above ground level?
why: Anything over 200 ft AGL needs Form 7460-1; closer to airports, imaginary-surface slopes set lower trigger heights.

q: What is the minimum size, in the smallest dimension, of an accessible elevator car control button?
why: Car and hall call buttons must be at least 3/4 in in their smallest dimension.

q: When accessible parking spaces are striped, where is their width measured?
c: From the inside edge of each line
From the outside edge of each line
From the centerline of the markings
why: Space and access aisle widths are measured to the centerline of the striping.

q: A 50,000 lb load hangs from a two-leg bridle with each leg at 45 degrees from horizontal. About how much tension is in each leg?
why: Each leg carries (W/2)/sin 45 = 0.707 x 50,000, about 35,400 lb; flatter angles raise leg tension.

q: Which of the following may NOT be used as a grounding electrode?
c: 20 ft of 1/2 in rebar encased in a footing
Metal underground water pipe with 10 ft in contact with earth
A ground ring of 2 AWG bare copper
why: Gas piping and aluminum are prohibited electrodes; concrete-encased rebar is permitted.

q: Under the IPC, what is the maximum horizontal support spacing for PVC pipe?
why: PVC and ABS are supported every 4 ft; small CPVC is 3 ft and PEX 32 in.

q: What minimum STC rating is required for walls separating dwelling units when tested in a lab?
why: Dwelling and sleeping unit separations need STC 50 (45 if field tested).

q: How many studs does a 12 ft straight partition need at 16 in on center, ignoring corners, openings and waste?
why: 144 in / 16 in = 9 spaces, plus 1 for the end stud, gives 10 studs.

q: A trench is 18 ft wide at the top, 5 ft wide at the bottom, 8 ft deep and 750 ft long. How much material is removed?
why: Average width (18+5)/2 = 11.5 ft x 8 ft x 750 ft = 69,000 cu ft.

q: What color marking identifies Type L copper water tube?
why: Type K is green, Type L blue and Type M red, from thickest to thinnest wall.

q: What is the maximum threshold height for a sliding door serving a dwelling unit?
why: Dwelling-unit sliding doors may have 3/4 in thresholds; other doors are limited to 1/2 in.

q: Untreated wood siding must be kept at least how far above the ground?
why: Wood within 6 in of earth, or within 2 in of exposed concrete, must be decay resistant or treated.

q: A building has a 1,600 sq ft basement with no sprinklers. Exterior openings intended to avoid the sprinkler requirement must each have a minimum dimension of at least:
why: Qualifying fire department access openings must be at least 30 in in their least dimension.

q: A contractor needs to store 650 lb of LP-gas outdoors in containers awaiting use. Under OSHA, what minimum distance must the storage be from the nearest building?
why: Quantities from 501 to 6,000 lb must be at least 10 ft from the nearest building; 20 ft applies above 6,000 lb and 25 ft above 10,000 lb.

q: What is the most flammable liquid OSHA allows to be kept in a single room on a construction site outside of an approved storage cabinet?
why: No more than 25 gallons of flammable liquid may be stored in a room outside an approved storage cabinet.

q: What is the minimum clearance between a scaffold and an insulated power line carrying less than 300 volts?
why: Insulated lines under 300 V require 3 ft of clearance; 300 V to 50 kV and uninsulated lines under 50 kV require 10 ft.

q: When a warning line system is used on a low-slope roof (no mechanical equipment), how far back from the roof edge must the line be placed at a minimum?
why: Warning lines must be at least 6 ft from the edge and flagged with high-visibility material at intervals of no more than 6 ft.

q: On a jobsite, a 2A-rated fire extinguisher is provided for each 3,000 sq ft. What is the maximum travel distance from any point to the nearest extinguisher?
why: OSHA limits travel distance to the nearest 2A extinguisher to 100 ft.

q: For plastering and lathing work, what is the maximum distance a scaffold platform may be from the face of the work?
why: The general limit is 14 in, but plastering and lathing operations are allowed up to 18 in.

q: What minimum rear clearance to combustibles does OSHA require for a temporary radiant-type room heater?
why: Radiant room heaters need 36 in at the sides and rear; circulating-type room heaters need only 12 in.

q: For an excavation less than 20 ft deep in Type B soil, what is OSHA's maximum allowable slope (horizontal to vertical)?
why: Type B soil may be sloped no steeper than 1H:1V (45 degrees); Type A is 3/4:1 and Type C is 1-1/2:1.

q: A loader moves 700 loose cubic yards per hour of soil with a 35 percent swell. About how many bank cubic yards per hour is that?
why: Bank volume equals loose volume divided by (1 + swell): 700 / 1.35 is about 519 BCY.

q: At a minimum, how often must the employer check a jobsite first aid kit once it is on the job?
why: The kit is checked before being sent to each job and at least weekly on each job so used items are replaced.

q: In OSHA excavation terms, what does a kickout describe?
c: A trench wall sliding into the excavation
Water boiling up through the trench bottom
Spoil rolling back into the trench
The accidental release or failure of a cross brace
why: OSHA defines kickout as the accidental release or failure of a cross brace in a shoring system.

q: Workers are in a trench 4 ft or more deep. What is the maximum lateral travel distance allowed to reach a ladder, stairway or ramp?
why: A means of egress must be located so no worker travels more than 25 ft laterally to reach it.

q: How far from the edge of an excavation must spoil piles be kept, at a minimum, when no retaining device is used?
why: Materials and equipment must be at least 2 ft from the excavation edge or held back by retaining devices.

q: A safety net is installed where the drop from the working level to the net is more than 10 ft. How far must the net extend outward from the outermost projection of the work surface?
why: Net extension is 8 ft for drops up to 5 ft, 10 ft for drops over 5 to 10 ft, and 13 ft for drops over 10 ft.

q: Above what oxygen concentration is a confined-space atmosphere considered oxygen-enriched?
why: Above 23.5 percent oxygen is oxygen-enriched; below 19.5 percent is oxygen-deficient.

q: When testing the atmosphere of a permit-required confined space before entry, what must be tested first?
why: Testing order is oxygen, then flammable gases and vapors, then toxic contaminants, since combustible gas meters need adequate oxygen to read correctly.

q: Under OSHA, compressed air may be used for cleaning only when its pressure is reduced below what level, with chip guarding and PPE?
why: Compressed air for cleaning must be under 30 psi and used only with effective chip guarding and PPE.

q: An anchorage for personal fall arrest, not designed by a qualified person, must support at least how much per attached employee?
why: Anchorages must hold 5,000 lb per employee or be designed with a safety factor of two under a qualified person's supervision.

q: What is the maximum height above the floor or ground at which a ladder jack scaffold may be used?
why: OSHA 1926.452(k)(1) limits ladder jack scaffold platforms to a height of 20 ft.

q: Hook-on ladders serving a supported scaffold more than 35 ft high must have rest platforms at what maximum vertical interval?
why: Rest platforms are required at vertical intervals of no more than 35 ft on these ladders.

q: What is the OSHA assigned protection factor for a full-facepiece air-purifying respirator?
why: A full-facepiece APR has an APF of 50, five times the APF of 10 for a half-mask APR.

q: What minimum depth of clear working space is required in front of an electrical panel operating at 120/240 V (150 V or less to ground)?
why: Under Table K-1, equipment at 0 to 150 V to ground needs 3 ft of working depth in front of it and at least 30 in of width; this is a distance, not an area.

q: What is the maximum slope permitted in any direction for an accessible parking space and its access aisle?
why: Parking spaces and access aisles may not exceed 1:48 (about 2 percent) in any direction.

q: An accessible ramp is built at a 1:12 slope. What is the maximum rise allowed for a single ramp run before a landing is required?
why: A ramp run may rise no more than 30 in; at 1:12 that is a 30 ft horizontal run.

q: What is the required height range for the top of an accessible water closet seat above the finished floor?
why: Accessible water closet seats must be 17 to 19 in above the floor, measured to the top of the seat.

q: What is the minimum clear width for an escalator serving a below-grade transportation station?
why: Escalators in below-grade stations must provide a clear width of at least 32 in.

q: Other than fire doors, what is the maximum force allowed to push or pull open an interior swinging door?
why: Interior swinging doors other than fire doors must open with no more than 5 lbf.

q: What is the minimum ceiling height required within a means of egress under the IBC?
why: Means of egress must have at least 7 ft 6 in of ceiling height, with limited exceptions such as 80 in stair headroom.

q: What is the maximum height from the floor to the bottom of the clear opening of a bedroom emergency escape and rescue opening?
why: The sill of an emergency escape and rescue opening may be no more than 44 in above the floor.

q: Absent a soils report, what presumptive allowable bearing pressure does the code assign to crystalline bedrock?
why: Crystalline bedrock is assigned 12,000 psf; sedimentary and foliated rock get 4,000 psf.

q: An asphalt parking area lies within 10 ft of a building foundation. What minimum slope away from the building is required?
why: Impervious surfaces within 10 ft of the foundation must slope at least 2 percent away from the building.

q: Before starting an excavation, how many days of advance written notice must be given to owners of adjoining buildings?
why: Notice must be delivered at least 10 days before the scheduled start so neighbors can protect their buildings.

q: An elevator hoistway enclosure connects five stories. What minimum fire-resistance rating does the shaft enclosure need?
why: Shafts connecting four or more stories need a 2-hour rating; fewer than four stories need 1 hour.

q: How far from the kitchen exhaust system must the manual actuation device for a commercial hood suppression system be located?
why: The manual pull must be on an egress path 10 to 20 ft from the exhaust system and 42 to 48 in above the floor.

q: Unless another section says otherwise, required emergency and standby power systems must run without refueling or recharging for at least how long?
why: The code's default load duration for emergency and standby power is 2 hours.

q: In a Type V building, a sidewall sprinkler protects an exterior deck of open wood joist construction. What is the maximum distance the deflector may be below the deck?
why: Deflectors may be 1 to 6 in below the structural members and no more than 14 in below the deck.

q: How far, at a minimum, must a smoke alarm be placed horizontally from the door of a bathroom containing a shower?
why: Smoke alarms must be at least 3 ft horizontally from the door or opening of a bathroom with a tub or shower, to limit steam nuisance alarms.

q: Which fastener material is acceptable for use in preservative-treated lumber under the IRC?
why: Fasteners in treated wood must be hot-dipped galvanized steel, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper.

q: What is the minimum overlap required where adjacent pieces of roof drip edge meet?
why: Drip edge segments must overlap at least 2 in and extend at least 2 in back onto the roof deck.

q: For a composite floor on formed steel deck, what minimum concrete thickness is required above the top of the deck flutes?
why: Composite design requires at least 2 in of concrete above the top of the steel deck.

q: Drywall takes 30 days, and painting may begin 7 days after drywall begins. How is this schedule relationship described?
why: Because the successor's start is tied to the predecessor's start plus 7 days, it is a start-to-start link with a 7-day lag.

q: A contractor assigns inflated values to early line items in the schedule of values. What is this practice called, and why is it done?
c: Back charging, to recover cleanup costs
Unbalanced bidding, to win the low bid
Front-end loading, to offset retainage and improve early cash flow
Value engineering, to lower the contract price
why: Front-end loading pulls payment forward into early pay applications, offsetting the cash withheld as retainage.

q: OSHA presumes certain flooring, insulation and surfacing materials contain asbestos in buildings constructed no later than what year?
why: Thermal insulation and surfacing in buildings built by 1980, and asphalt or vinyl flooring installed by 1980, are presumed asbestos-containing unless tested.

q: Under the IRC, at what header span must the header joist and trimmer joists around a floor opening be doubled?
why: Header spans over 4 ft require doubled header and trimmers; spans over 6 ft also require hangers.

q: A portable ladder gives access to an upper landing. How far must its side rails extend above the landing surface?
why: Side rails must extend at least 3 ft above the upper landing unless a grab device is provided where that is not possible.

q: In a dwelling, 15- and 20-amp, 125-volt receptacles within what distance of the top inside edge of a sink bowl require GFCI protection?
why: Receptacles within 6 ft of the top inside edge of a sink bowl must be GFCI-protected.

q: About how many threads are cut on the end of a 1/2 in steel gas pipe?
why: The IFGC threading table calls for about 10 threads (roughly 3/4 in of thread) on 1/2 in and 3/4 in pipe.

q: On a topographic site map, what do contour lines spaced very close together indicate?
why: Each contour is a fixed elevation interval, so closely spaced lines mean elevation changes quickly over a short distance.

q: A notch is needed in the bottom edge of a sawn-lumber floor joist, outside the middle third of the span and away from the bearing. What is the maximum notch depth?
why: Notches away from the ends are limited to 1/6 of the joist depth and are not allowed in the middle third; only end notches may go to 1/4 of the depth.

q: Where collar ties connect opposing rafters, what is the maximum spacing permitted by the IRC?
why: Collar ties must be at least 1x4, in the upper third of the attic, and no more than 4 ft apart, which is every third pair of rafters set 16 in on center.

q: In a crawl space, untreated wood floor joists must be at least how far above exposed ground?
why: Joists closer than 18 in (girders closer than 12 in) to exposed ground must be naturally durable or preservative-treated wood.

q: A 2x4 strut supporting a roof purlin runs down to a bearing wall at a slope of at least 45 degrees. What is the maximum unbraced length of the strut?
why: Purlin struts are limited to 8 ft of unbraced length, spaced no more than 4 ft on center, at a slope of at least 45 degrees.

q: Minimum embedment of 1/2-in anchor bolts securing a sill plate to a concrete foundation is:
why: Bolts must be embedded at least 7 in, spaced no more than 6 ft apart, with a bolt within 12 in of each plate end.

q: High-early-strength concrete must be kept above 50 degrees F and moist for at least how long after placement?
why: High-early-strength concrete needs at least 3 days of curing; ordinary concrete needs at least 7 days.

q: Per ACI 347, what minimum construction live load is added to the slab dead load when designing elevated slab formwork (no motorized carts)?
why: The minimum construction live load is 50 psf (75 psf with motorized carts), and dead plus live load must total at least 100 psf.

q: A slab on grade is 5 in thick. What is the minimum depth for its saw-cut contraction joints?
why: Contraction joints should be at least 1/4 of the slab thickness, and 5 in x 1/4 = 1-1/4 in.

q: What is the nominal diameter of a #6 reinforcing bar?
why: Inch-pound bar numbers give the diameter in eighths of an inch, so #6 = 6/8 = 0.75 in.

q: Weld washers are required when puddle welding steel deck thinner than:
why: Deck thinner than 0.028 in will burn through under an arc spot weld, so a weld washer is used to make the connection.

q: Under the AIA A201 general conditions, unless the contract documents provide otherwise, who secures and pays for the building permit?
why: A201 puts the contractor in charge of the building permit and other legally required permits, fees, licenses and inspections, unless the contract says otherwise.

q: A non-exempt carpenter works 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, and must answer the office phone during a 30-minute clocked-out lunch each day. Under the FLSA, how should the lunch time be paid?
c: It is unpaid because meal periods are never compensable
5 hours at 1.5 times the regular rate
2.5 hours at 1.5 times the regular rate
why: A meal break is unpaid only if the employee is fully relieved of duty; the 5 x 0.5 = 2.5 hours push the week past 40, so they are paid as overtime.

q: Which document proves employment authorization but not identity for Form I-9 purposes?
why: A Social Security card is a List C document and must be paired with a List B identity document; a passport or green card is List A and proves both.

q: How long must an employer keep its OSHA 300 log, 300A summary and 301 incident reports?
c: 5 years after the end of the calendar year covered
1 year after the end of the calendar year covered
3 years from the date of each injury
30 years from the date of each injury
why: Injury and illness records are kept 5 years after the year they cover; the 30-year rule applies to exposure and medical records.

q: What rate of Social Security tax is withheld from an employee's wages (up to the annual wage base)?
why: The employee pays 6.2% and the employer matches 6.2%, for 12.4% in total; 1.45% is the Medicare rate.

q: To be eligible for FMLA leave, an employee must have worked at least how many hours for the employer during the previous 12 months?
why: Eligibility requires 12 months of employment, 1,250 hours in the past 12 months, and 50 employees within 75 miles.

q: Under IBC 2021, swinging doors serving a Group H occupancy must have panic or fire exit hardware when the occupant load reaches:
c: Any occupant load; no threshold applies
why: Group H requires panic or fire exit hardware whatever the occupant load; the 50-person trigger applies to Group A and E spaces.

q: An elevator shaft connects three stories. What is its minimum fire-resistance rating (assuming the floors penetrated are rated no more than that)?
why: Shafts connecting fewer than four stories need 1 hour; four or more stories need 2 hours, and never less than the floor penetrated.

q: Where only one elevator is installed and standby power is required, the elevator must transfer to standby power within what time after normal power fails?
why: A single elevator must switch to standby power automatically within 60 seconds of losing normal power.

q: What is the minimum fire protection rating for a door in a fire-resistance-rated corridor wall?
why: Doors in rated corridor walls need a 1/3-hour (20-minute) rating and must also meet smoke and draft control requirements.

q: What is the minimum clearance between the floor and the bottom of a wall-mounted hand-held portable fire extinguisher?
why: At least 4 in of clearance is required below the extinguisher; the top may be no higher than 5 ft for units of 40 lb or less.

q: A van-accessible parking space served by a 60-in access aisle must be at least how wide?
why: A van space is 132 in wide with a 60-in aisle, or 96 in wide if the aisle is at least 96 in.

q: What is the steepest cross slope allowed on an accessible ramp run or landing?
why: A cross slope of no more than 1:48 lets water drain without making wheelchairs drift sideways; 1:12 is the maximum running slope.

q: Handrails are required on both sides of an accessible ramp run when its rise is greater than:
why: Ramp runs rising more than 6 in need handrails on both sides; circular handrails must be 1-1/4 to 2 in in diameter.

q: A 3/8-in change in level on an accessible route will be beveled. What is the steepest bevel allowed?
why: Changes from 1/4 in to 1/2 in may be beveled at no more than 1:2; over 1/2 in requires a ramp.

q: Midrails, screens or mesh are required in a guardrail system unless there is a wall or parapet at least how high?
why: Intermediate members are needed between the top rail and the walking surface wherever no wall or parapet at least 21 in high exists.

q: An owner holds three separate contracts, one each with the architect, the general contractor, and a construction manager who serves only as the owner's advisor. Which delivery method is this?
why: In agency CM the construction manager advises the owner without taking cost risk, and the owner contracts directly with both the designer and the contractor.

q: Without a geotechnical report, what is the IBC presumptive allowable foundation pressure for sandy gravel or gravel (GW, GP)?
why: Gravels get 3,000 psf, sands and silty/clayey sands 2,000 psf, and clays and silts 1,500 psf.

q: Under the IBC, interior wall finish is set on wood furring over a fire-resistance-rated or noncombustible wall. If the space behind the finish is not filled with inorganic or Class A material, fireblocking is required at what maximum interval in any direction?
why: IBC 803 requires furred spaces behind finish on rated or noncombustible elements to be filled with inorganic or Class A material or fireblocked (per Section 718) at no more than 8 ft in any direction.

q: What is the minimum depth of a footing below undisturbed ground surface (before considering frost depth)?
why: Footings go at least 12 in below undisturbed ground and also below the frost line unless they are frost-protected.

q: An owner pays a progress payment one day late. The contractor stops all work and walks off the job with no intent to return. Legally, which statement is correct?
c: The contractor has committed a material breach
The owner committed a material breach that justified termination
Neither party has breached the contract
The contractor committed only a minor breach
why: A one-day-late payment is a minor breach that allows only damages; abandoning the job is a material breach by the contractor.

q: In Type I or II construction, a skylight sloped less than 45 degrees from horizontal must be mounted on a curb at least how high above the roof plane?
why: These skylights need a curb at least 4 in high, and in Types I and II their frames must be noncombustible.

q: A jobsite has 25 workers. Under OSHA, what is the minimum toilet facility requirement?
why: With 20 or more workers, OSHA requires 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 40 workers, so 25 workers need one of each.

q: What is the maximum daily exposure OSHA permits for continuous noise at 95 dBA?
why: Table D-2 allows 4 hours at 95 dBA; the permitted time halves for every 5 dBA increase above 90 dBA.

q: A worker is exposed to 105 dBA for 30 minutes and 92 dBA for 4 hours. What is the combined noise dose?
why: 0.5 h / 1 h at 105 dBA = 0.50 plus 4 h / 6 h at 92 dBA = 0.67, totaling 1.17; any total above 1 exceeds the permissible exposure.

q: OSHA Table D-3 has a row titled 'general construction area lighting' (overall site lighting). What minimum illumination does that row require?
why: The 'general construction area lighting' row is 5 foot-candles. A separate 3 foot-candle row covers general construction areas, concrete placement, excavation and waste areas, accessways, active storage, loading platforms, refueling and field maintenance; shops need 10 and offices or first aid stations 30.

q: A personal fall arrest system must be rigged so that a worker cannot free fall more than:
why: PFAS must limit free fall to 6 ft and prevent contact with any lower level, using a full body harness rather than a body belt.

q: A safety net is hung 8 ft below the working surface. How far must it extend horizontally beyond the edge of the work surface?
why: Nets more than 5 ft and up to 10 ft below the work surface must extend 10 ft; 8 ft applies only up to 5 ft below and 13 ft beyond 10 ft.

q: On a building under construction, one fire extinguisher rated at least 2A must be provided for each how many square feet of protected area?
why: OSHA requires a 2A extinguisher per 3,000 sq ft with no more than 100 ft of travel to reach one; a 55-gallon drum with two pails may substitute.

q: Which extinguisher type is NOT suitable for a gasoline or grease (Class B) fire?
why: Soda-acid is a water-based agent rated only for Class A fires; water spreads burning liquids, so Class B fires need CO2, dry chemical or foam.

q: What is the maximum amount of Category 4 flammable liquid allowed in one approved storage cabinet?
why: A cabinet may hold 60 gallons of Category 1-3 liquids or 120 gallons of Category 4 liquids.

q: How far must a temporary heater be kept from combustible tarpaulins or canvas coverings?
why: Heaters used near combustible tarps, canvas or similar coverings must be at least 10 ft away to prevent ignition.

q: Materials stored inside a building under construction may not be placed within what distance of a hoistway or inside floor opening?
why: Stored material must stay 6 ft from hoistways and floor openings, and 10 ft from an exterior wall that does not extend above the material.

q: What is the maximum height of a loose brick stack on a jobsite?
why: Loose brick stacks are limited to 7 ft and must taper back 2 in per foot of height above 4 ft.

q: Materials are being dropped to a point outside the exterior walls of a building. Above what drop height is an enclosed chute required?
why: An enclosed chute is required whenever material is dropped more than 20 ft to a point outside the building's exterior walls.

q: Debris is dropped through a floor opening without a chute. What barricade is required around the landing area?
c: 36 in high, 4 ft back from the opening edge
42 in high, 6 ft back from the opening edge
42 in high, 10 ft back from the opening edge
48 in high, 6 ft back from the opening edge
why: The drop area must be fully enclosed by barricades at least 42 in high and at least 6 ft back from the projected edge of the opening, with warning signs at each level.

q: Compressed air may be used for cleaning only when its pressure is reduced to:
why: Cleaning air must be below 30 psi and used only with effective chip guarding and PPE.

q: On a bench or floor-stand grinder, the exposed portion of the wheel periphery and sides may not exceed what angle for normal work above the spindle?
why: Guards may expose no more than 90 degrees of the wheel, increasing to 125 degrees only when work must contact the wheel below the spindle centerline.

q: Stored oxygen cylinders must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders by a minimum distance of:
why: Separation must be at least 20 ft, or a noncombustible barrier at least 5 ft high with at least a one-half hour fire rating.

q: Each scaffold and scaffold component must be able to support its own weight plus at least how many times the maximum intended load?
why: Scaffold components need a 4-to-1 factor; suspension ropes need 6 times the maximum intended load.

q: What is the maximum platform height permitted on a ladder jack scaffold?
why: Ladder jack scaffold platforms may not exceed 20 ft in height.

q: OSHA's non-mandatory scaffold specifications (Appendix A to Subpart L) describe float (ship) scaffolds for a maximum intended load of:
why: Appendix A gives float scaffold specifications (3/4 in plywood platform, 2x4 or 1x10 bearers, rope equal to 1 in manila) for a 750 lb maximum intended load; the mandatory rule in 1926.452(s) has no load figure.

q: During overhand bricklaying, fall protection is required when a mason reaches more than what distance below the walking/working surface?
why: Reaching more than 10 in below the working level requires guardrails, safety nets or personal fall arrest.

q: What is the required height of a guardrail top rail above the walking/working level?
why: Top rails must be 42 in plus or minus 3 in high and withstand a 200 lb force; midrails go midway between top rail and surface.

q: What is the minimum breaking strength for lanyards and vertical lifelines in a personal fall arrest system?
why: Lanyards and vertical lifelines need at least 5,000 lb breaking strength, matching the 5,000 lb per-person anchorage requirement.

q: A cover over a floor hole must be able to support at least:
why: Hole covers must support twice the weight of workers, equipment and materials that may be on them at one time, and must be secured and marked.

q: During roofing work without guardrails at the edge, materials may not be stored within what distance of the roof edge?
why: Construction roofing rules bar storing materials and equipment within 6 ft of a roof edge unless guardrails are erected there.

q: OSHA 1926.602(a)(5), whose fender requirement is currently suspended, applies to rubber-tired earthmoving haulage equipment whose maximum speed exceeds:
why: The rule covers pneumatic-tired trucks, scrapers, tractors and trailing units capable of more than 15 mph, but 1926.602(a)(8)(ii) suspends the fender requirement pending reconsideration.

q: In a trench protected by a shield (trench box), how far below the bottom of the shield may soil be excavated if conditions allow?
why: Up to 2 ft below the shield is allowed only if the shield is designed for the full trench depth and there is no sign of soil loss.

q: What is the maximum allowable slope (horizontal to vertical) for a simple sloped excavation 20 ft deep or less in Type C soil?
why: Type C soil requires 1-1/2:1 (34 degrees); Type B is 1:1 and Type A is 3/4:1.

q: A 12 ft high masonry wall is under construction. How wide must the limited access zone be?
why: The limited access zone equals the wall height plus 4 ft and runs the full length of the wall on the unscaffolded side.

q: Before steel erection begins, the erector must receive written notice that footing and pier concrete has reached what portion of its minimum design strength?
why: Concrete must reach 75 percent of intended minimum compressive strength (or enough to carry erection loads), confirmed in writing.

q: What is the minimum number of anchor rods required for each steel column?
why: All columns must be anchored with at least 4 anchor rods to resist overturning during erection.

q: Apart from connectors and controlled decking zones, steel erection workers need fall protection when on an unprotected edge more than how high above a lower level?
why: Subpart R sets 15 ft for steel erection; connectors and decking zone workers are protected at more than two stories or 30 ft.

q: How much fresh air must be supplied for each employee working underground?
why: Underground ventilation must supply at least 200 cubic feet per minute of fresh air per employee.

q: Within what range of angles from horizontal must construction stairways be installed?
why: Stairs must be between 30 and 50 degrees from horizontal; a stair or ladder is needed at any break in elevation of 19 in or more.

q: In what order must a confined space atmosphere be tested before entry?
why: Test oxygen first (sensors for combustibles need oxygen to read correctly), then flammable gases and vapors, then toxic contaminants.

q: What is the OSHA 8-hour time-weighted average permissible exposure limit for asbestos in construction?
why: The PEL is 0.1 fiber/cc as an 8-hour TWA; 1.0 fiber/cc over 30 minutes is the excursion limit.

q: The utility has confirmed a nearby power line is 45 kV. What minimum clearance must a crane and its load keep from the line?
why: Table A requires 10 ft for lines up to 50 kV once the voltage is confirmed; without confirmation the default is 20 ft for lines up to 350 kV.

q: A crane will exceed FAA notice criteria near a public-use airport. At least how far in advance must FAA Form 7460-1 be filed?
why: Part 77 requires notice at least 45 days before construction or crane use that meets the notice criteria.

q: When lifting a truss longer than 60 ft, the strongback or spreader bar should be about what fraction of the truss length?
why: Long trusses over 60 ft need a strongback or spreader bar about 2/3 to 3/4 of their length to prevent lateral bending.

q: During truss erection, diagonal bracing must be installed at each end of the building and repeated at what interval?
why: Diagonal bracing anchors the lateral restraint rows and is repeated every 10 truss spaces, no more than 20 ft apart.

q: Rows of bottom chord temporary lateral restraint (BCTLR) should be spaced no more than:
why: BCSI calls for BCTLR rows at a maximum of 15 ft on center, tied to diagonal bracing.

q: How many board feet are in a 2 in x 12 in plank that is 14 ft long?
why: Board feet = thickness x width (inches) x length (feet) / 12, so 2 x 12 x 14 / 12 = 28.

q: A basement excavation measures 30 ft by 40 ft by 3 ft deep. About how many cubic yards of earth must be removed?
why: 30 x 40 x 3 = 3,600 cu ft, and 3,600 / 27 = about 133 cu yd.

q: Adding water to a concrete mix without adding cement will most directly:
why: A higher water-cement ratio weakens the hardened paste, reducing strength, durability and watertightness, and raises slump.

q: In weather of 80 degrees F or warmer, mortar should be used within about how long after mixing?
why: Mortar should be placed within about 2-1/2 hours of mixing; it may be retempered only for evaporation, never after it begins to set.

q: Under the IRC, notches in solid sawn floor joists are prohibited in which part of the span?
c: The first 2 ft from a bearing
The middle third of the span
The outer quarter at each end
The top edge near the bearing
why: Notches may not be in the middle third of the span, where bending stress is highest, and are limited to 1/6 of the joist depth.

q: What minimum bearing length does the IRC require for ceiling joist ends resting on a masonry wall?
why: Joists need 3 in of bearing on masonry or concrete and 1-1/2 in on wood or metal.

q: In concealed spaces of wood stud walls, horizontal fireblocking is required at intervals not exceeding:
why: Fireblocking goes at ceiling and floor levels and horizontally at no more than 10 ft intervals to slow fire spread through cavities.

q: What is the length of a 16d common nail?
why: Penny size indicates length: 8d is 2-1/2 in, 10d is 3 in and 16d is 3-1/2 in.

q: A level rod reads 5 ft at point A and 7 ft at point B. What is the relationship between the two points?
c: B is 2 ft higher than A
Both points are at the same elevation
B is 2 ft lower than A
B is 12 ft lower than A
why: A larger rod reading means the ground is farther below the line of sight, so B is 7 - 5 = 2 ft lower.

q: A general contractor holds the prime contract for a building and subcontracts all of the framing. Under OSHA's construction standards, who is responsible for safety compliance on the framing work?
c: Only the framing subcontractor, because it controls the work
The prime contractor, which keeps overall responsibility, along with the framing subcontractor for its portion
Only the owner, who holds the building permit
The prime contractor only if the subcontract assigns safety to it in writing
why: By contracting for full performance, the prime contractor assumes all employer obligations for the whole job, even subcontracted work. Each subcontractor is also responsible for its own portion.

q: A rigging wire rope must be removed from service when the visible broken wires in any length of eight rope diameters exceed what share of the total wires?
why: Wire rope is retired when broken wires in any length of eight diameters exceed 10 percent of the total wires, or when it shows other excessive wear, corrosion or defects.

q: Which type of control must a hand-held powered circular saw have so that the power shuts off when the operator lets go?
c: Lock-on switch with a separate release button
why: Circular saws, chain saws and percussion tools without positive accessory holding means need a constant-pressure switch that cuts the power when it is released.

q: Inside a building under construction, compressed gas cylinders must be stored at least how far from highly combustible materials such as oil or excelsior?
why: Indoor cylinder storage must be well-protected, ventilated and dry, and at least 20 ft (6.1 m) from highly combustible materials.

q: An electrician will work on 480Y/277-volt equipment (277 V to ground) with exposed live parts on one side of the working space and a concrete block wall on the other. What is the minimum depth of clear working space?
why: For 151 to 600 volts to ground, live parts on one side with grounded parts opposite require 3-1/2 ft, and concrete, brick or tile walls count as grounded.

q: What is the maximum distance allowed between an outrigger scaffold platform and the face of the work?
why: Outrigger scaffolds are limited to 3 in from the face. The 14 in general limit and 18 in plastering/lathing limit do not apply to them.

q: Unless it is cleated or otherwise restrained, each end of a scaffold platform must extend past the centerline of its support by at least
why: An unrestrained platform end must extend at least 6 in over the centerline of its support so it cannot slip off.

q: Under what condition may a forklift be used to support a scaffold platform?
c: Never; forklifts are prohibited from supporting platforms
When the forks are lowered to within 6 ft of the ground
When the entire platform is attached to the forks and the forklift does not move horizontally while the platform is occupied
When a spotter stays at the forklift at all times
why: A forklift may hold a scaffold platform only if the whole platform is attached to the fork and the forklift is not moved horizontally while workers are on it.

q: Workers on a scaffold must be protected from falling once they are more than what height above a lower level?
why: The scaffold standard sets the fall protection trigger at more than 10 ft, unlike the 6 ft general trigger in Subpart M.

q: On a supported scaffold placed in service after January 1, 2000, the top edge of the toprail must be between which heights above the platform?
why: Newer supported scaffolds need toprails 38 to 45 in high. The 36 to 45 in range applies only to older supported scaffolds and certain suspended scaffolds.

q: A wall opening has its outside bottom edge 8 ft above the ground. Fall protection is required if the inside bottom edge is less than how high above the floor?
why: Wall openings need guardrails, nets or fall arrest when the outside drop is 6 ft or more and the inside bottom edge is less than 39 in above the walking surface.

q: When balusters are used as intermediate members in a guardrail system, they may be no more than how far apart?
why: Intermediate members such as balusters may be at most 19 in apart, and no opening in the guardrail system may exceed 19 in.

q: A safety net installation that stays in one place must be drop-tested again at intervals of no more than
why: Nets are drop-tested after installation, relocation and major repair, and every 6 months if left in place, using a 400 lb sand bag.

q: A temporary cover over a hole in a vehicle aisle must support, without failure, at least
c: the gross weight of the heaviest vehicle expected
twice the maximum axle load of the largest vehicle expected to cross it
1.5 times the weight of workers and materials on it
4 times the intended load of foot traffic
why: Covers in roadways and vehicle aisles must carry at least twice the maximum axle load of the largest vehicle expected. Other covers must carry twice the load of workers, equipment and materials.

q: Where a hazardous atmosphere could reasonably be expected, such as an excavation in a former landfill, the air must be tested before workers enter excavations deeper than
why: Atmospheric testing is required before entry into excavations greater than 4 ft deep where oxygen deficiency or a hazardous atmosphere may exist.

q: A cohesive soil has an unconfined compressive strength of 2 tsf. Which condition by itself keeps it from being classified as Type A?
c: It was excavated less than 24 hours ago
why: No soil is Type A if it is fissured, subject to vibration, previously disturbed, or in layers dipping into the excavation at 4H:1V or steeper. Clay loam and cemented soils can be Type A.

q: An excavation in Type A soil is 10 ft deep and will be open less than 24 hours. What is the steepest simple slope Appendix B allows?
why: Short-term (24 hours or less) Type A excavations 12 ft deep or less may be sloped at 1/2H:1V. Otherwise Type A is limited to 3/4H:1V.

q: During multi-story steel erection, unfinished bolting or welding above the foundation or uppermost permanently secured floor may not exceed
c: 2 floors or 30 ft, whichever is less
4 floors or 48 ft, whichever is less
8 floors or 96 ft, whichever is less
4 floors or 48 ft, whichever is greater
why: The limit is 4 floors or 48 ft, whichever is less, unless the design maintains structural integrity. The 2 stories or 30 ft figure applies to the decked floor or nets below erection work.

q: A bundle of joist bridging landed on steel joists may weigh no more than
why: Bridging bundles are capped at 1,000 lb and must sit on at least 3 joists secured at one end, within 1 ft of the secured end.

q: An extra-heavy-duty Type 1A metal or plastic portable ladder must be able to support at least how many times its maximum intended load?
why: Portable ladders generally must hold 4 times the maximum intended load, but Type 1A metal or plastic ladders need only 3.3 times.

q: An extension ladder has a working length of 20 ft from its foot to its top support. About how far out from the support should its foot be placed?
why: The horizontal distance should be about one-quarter of the working length, and 20 ft / 4 = 5 ft.

q: A soil swells 25 percent when excavated. What is its load factor?
why: Load factor = 1 / (1 + swell) = 1 / 1.25 = 0.80. Multiply loose volume by it to get bank volume.

q: You must haul away 1,000 bank cubic yards of soil that swells 32 percent, using trucks that carry 14 loose cubic yards. How many truck trips are needed?
why: 1,000 BCY x 1.32 = 1,320 LCY, and 1,320 / 14 = 94.3. A partial load still needs a trip, so round up to 95.

q: On a site plan, station 6+75 is how far from station 0+00?
why: One full station is 100 ft, so 6+75 means 6 x 100 + 75 = 675 ft from the start.

q: In the standard Proctor compaction test (ASTM D698), each soil layer gets 25 blows from a rammer of what weight dropped from what height?
why: Standard Proctor uses a 5.5 lb rammer dropped 12 in on 3 layers. The 10 lb rammer dropped 18 in on 5 layers is the modified Proctor test.

q: Under AISC standard hole sizes, what diameter hole is used for a 1 in diameter structural bolt?
why: Standard holes are the bolt diameter plus 1/16 in for bolts under 1 in, but plus 1/8 in for bolts 1 in and larger.

q: In the steel designation W12x26, what does the number 26 indicate?
c: Weight in pounds per linear foot
Length of the member in feet
why: W shapes are designated by nominal depth (12 in) followed by weight per foot (26 lb/ft).

q: How are field seams in an EPDM single-ply roof membrane normally joined?
c: Lapping with splice adhesive or seam tape
why: EPDM is a thermoset rubber that cannot be heat-welded, so its laps are bonded with adhesive or tape. Heat welding is used for thermoplastics such as PVC and TPO.

q: Which statement best describes a curtain wall?
c: An exterior wall that carries floor and roof loads to the foundation
A non-load-bearing exterior wall that carries its own weight and wind loads to the frame
An interior fire wall that divides a building into separate areas
A temporary wall used to brace masonry during construction
why: A curtain wall supports only itself and the lateral loads on it. A wall that carries floor or roof loads is a bearing wall.

q: Along a simply supported reinforced concrete beam, where are stirrups normally spaced closest together?
c: Only within the top third of the beam depth
why: Shear and diagonal tension are highest near the supports, so stirrups are closest together there and spread out toward midspan.

q: Unless the drawings say otherwise, what minimum concrete cover is required over the reinforcement in a footing cast directly against and permanently exposed to the earth?
why: Concrete cast against and permanently exposed to earth needs 3 in of cover; the 2-in and 1-1/2-in values apply to formed surfaces exposed to weather or soil.

q: Deformed shrinkage-and-temperature bars in a 6-in-thick structural slab may be spaced no farther apart than:
why: T&S bar spacing is limited to the lesser of 5 times the slab thickness (30 in here) and 18 in, so 18 in governs.

q: An inspector checks reinforcing bars just before a pour. Which condition requires the bars to be cleaned before concrete is placed?
c: Light, tight rust on the bar surface
Mill scale left from the rolling process
Minor seams that still meet ASTM limits
Form oil and dried mud on the bars
why: Mud, oil and similar coatings impair bond and must be removed; ordinary rust and mill scale are acceptable if a wire-brushed sample still meets ASTM minimums.

q: Strip shingles 12 in wide are installed with a 5-in exposure. What is the head lap?
why: Head lap equals shingle width minus twice the exposure: 12 - (2 x 5) = 2 in. The 7-in figure is the top lap (width minus exposure).

q: On an asphalt shingle roof with an open valley lined with corrosion-resistant metal, the valley lining must be at least how wide?
why: Metal open-valley lining must be at least 24 in wide; 18 in is the bottom ply width when two plies of mineral-surfaced roll roofing are used instead.

q: Under the IRC, a Class II vapor retarder, such as the kraft facing on batt insulation, has a permeance of:
why: Class I is 0.1 perm or less, Class II is over 0.1 to 1.0 perm, and Class III is over 1.0 to 10 perm.

q: For an egress stairway in a commercial office building, the IBC limits riser height to:
why: Egress stair risers must be 4 to 7 in high with treads at least 11 in deep; the 7-3/4 in maximum applies only in Group R-3 and inside dwelling units.

q: Egress lighting on emergency power is allowed to dim over its required 90-minute duration. At the end of that period, what average illumination must still be provided along the path of egress at floor level?
why: Emergency egress lighting starts at a 1-fc average (0.1-fc minimum) and may decline to a 0.6-fc average and 0.06-fc minimum by the end of the duration.

q: An area of refuge serves spaces with a combined occupant load of 450. How many 30 x 48 in wheelchair spaces must it provide?
why: One wheelchair space is required per 200 occupants or portion thereof: 450 / 200 = 2.25, which rounds up to 3.

q: Fire protection may be left off the bottom flange of a lintel that is part of the primary structural frame when the lintel spans no more than:
why: Bottom-flange protection is not required for lintels, shelf angles and plates spanning 6 ft 4 in or less, or for those outside the primary frame at any span.

q: A means-of-egress ramp built at the steepest running slope the IBC permits has a grade of approximately:
why: The maximum ramp slope is 1:12. The IBC text labels this an '8-percent slope', but 1 divided by 12 is about 8.33 percent, the closest choice. 5 percent (1:20) is the point above which a walking surface is treated as a ramp.

q: In which delivery method does a construction manager advise the owner during design and then hold the trade contracts under a guaranteed maximum price?
why: In CM at risk the CM takes on contract and cost risk, usually under a GMP; an agency CM only advises the owner and holds no trade contracts.

q: Which AIA form does a contractor commonly submit each month as its Application and Certificate for Payment?
why: G702 is the payment application, backed by the G703 continuation sheet; A101 is an owner-contractor agreement, A201 the general conditions, and G704 the certificate of substantial completion.

q: A project manager splits the full project scope into smaller deliverable-based work packages, each assigned to a responsible person with its own duration and cost. This tool is the:
why: A WBS breaks the scope into manageable, measurable work packages; it feeds the schedule and estimate but is not itself a schedule or a billing document.

q: A contractor is bidding a federally funded repair job on a public courthouse. Above what contract amount do the Davis-Bacon Act's prevailing wage requirements apply?
why: Davis-Bacon covers federally funded or assisted construction, alteration and repair contracts over $2,000, a statutory figure that is not adjusted for inflation. $2,500 is the Service Contract Act threshold. $15,000 was the Walsh-Healey supply-contract threshold until an October 2025 FAR inflation adjustment raised it to $20,000, and $150,000 was the Miller Act bond threshold as of 2025.
