q: Two days after reporting an unshored trench to OSHA, a laborer is moved to night shifts at lower pay. To pursue a Section 11(c) retaliation claim, he must file a complaint with OSHA within:
why: Section 11(c) of the OSH Act gives employees 30 days from the retaliatory action to file; other whistleblower laws OSHA enforces have different deadlines.

q: A contractor makes its employment tax deposit 9 calendar days after the due date. What failure-to-deposit penalty rate applies to the late amount?
why: Deposits 1-5 days late draw 2%, 6-15 days late 5%, more than 15 days late 10%, and amounts still unpaid more than 10 days after the first IRS notice 15%.

q: A contractor's CGL policy (no endorsements) has a $500 per-occurrence deductible. One crane accident causes $4,200 in injuries to two of the contractor's laborers, $3,600 damage to a neighbor's parked car, $2,900 damage to scaffolding the contractor owns and $1,800 loss of lumber the contractor bought for the job. How much does the CGL insurer pay?
ref: ISO CG 00 01 exclusions e and j
why: CGL covers only third-party injury or damage, so only the $3,600 car claim counts, less the $500 deductible. Employee injuries go to workers' comp, and the contractor's own scaffolding and lumber are excluded owned property.

q: A contractor's workers' compensation rates are $0.15 per $100 of clerical payroll and $4.00 per $100 of carpentry payroll. Annual payroll is $40,000 clerical and $150,000 carpentry, and the insurer gives a 10% credit for a written safety program. What is the annual premium?
why: Clerical: 400 x $0.15 = $60; carpentry: 1,500 x $4.00 = $6,000; total $6,060 less the 10% credit = $5,454. Rates apply per $100 of payroll in each class.

q: A non-exempt carpenter paid $22.00 per hour works 47 hours in one workweek. What is the overtime premium portion of his pay?
why: The premium is the extra half-time on hours over 40: 7 hours x $11.00 = $77. His total gross pay would be 47 x $22 + $77 = $1,111.

q: In a CPM schedule an activity has an early start of day 12, a late start of day 15, an early finish of day 20 and a late finish of day 23. How much total float does it have?
why: Total float is late finish minus early finish (23 - 20) or late start minus early start (15 - 12): 3 days the activity can slip without delaying project completion.

q: A three-member general partnership made a profit last year. Which federal return must the partnership itself file to report its income and each partner's share?
why: A partnership pays no federal income tax but must file the Form 1065 information return every year and issue each partner a Schedule K-1. Form 1120 is for C corporations, 1120-S for S corporations and Schedule C for sole proprietors.

q: A sole proprietor owes self-employment tax once net earnings from self-employment for the year reach at least:
why: Self-employment tax (15.3% for Social Security and Medicare) applies when net self-employment earnings are $400 or more; it is figured on Schedule SE and filed with Form 1040.

q: A subcontract clause excuses late completion caused by events beyond either party's control, such as a regional trade strike or a hurricane. This is a:
why: A force majeure clause shields a party from liability for delay caused by events it cannot control, usually by granting extra time. A liquidated damages clause does the opposite, charging a set amount per day of late completion.

q: What is the maximum number of shareholders an S corporation may have?
why: An S corporation is limited to 100 shareholders (family members may count as one) and one class of stock; a C corporation has no shareholder limit.

q: A new hire wants to present only one document for Form I-9. Which one is acceptable by itself to prove both identity and employment authorization?
why: A U.S. passport or passport card is a List A document. A state ID or voter registration card is List B (identity only) and a birth certificate is List C (work authorization only), so each must be paired with a document from the other list.
